transcript: Do I have any West End pics for the next coming months? Well, yes, I do, because I just booked my flight to London yesterday. Obviously the hot ticket this year is Paddington. Everybody is seeing it. It is freaking sold out. I know people who have had luck on Twickets, which is like their kind of theatre app in London, so definitely check that out if you don't already have tickets to Paddington. I bought my ticket before I even knew I was taking a trip to London. I just was like, I'll just grab a ticket and we'll figure it out later. I am also really excited for their production of into the Woods. It looks incredibly dark, and I just love into the woods in general. That's at the Bridge Theatre. They also have the production of American Psycho that I really wanna see because I've never seen that musical. It is at the Almeida Theatre, which is very tiny. The run sold out. But again, sometimes you have luck on twickets. And then you have The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry, which I think Paddington's getting kind of all of the love this year. But I have heard so many good things about Harold Fry that that, for me, was the front runner for the Olivier until Paddington opened. So definitely check that out. It's only playing until, I believe, April. There's also some interesting plays like, uh, Dracula, which is done by the same person. That did picture of Dorian Gray. Same kind of technology. It's a one person show starring now Cynthia erivo, with a bunch of camera people and technicians making some theatrical magic happen. Not my favourite kind of storytelling, but people loved it. So if that was your thing, definitely go see Dracula. Uh, I also am probably gonna go see Arcadia. I've never seen a production of Arcadia. It's a Tom Stoppard play that everyone loves. I've heard nothing but good things about the play in general, so I definitely need to see a production of it. That, that's at the Old Vic, inter alia, is returning, which I absolutely adored. Another play by the same writer as prima facie, this one starring Rosamund Pike. Fantastic play. And I always recommend looking at some of the smaller theatres like the Kiln, like Southwark Playhouse even some other theatres outside of West End and the big name London Theatres. I'm really excited for Ballad Lines, which is at Southwark Playhouse. Midnight's is Toddrick Hall's new musical that's premiering that I'm really excited for. And then, uh, Maimuna Memon has a show, Manic Street Creature, that's only playing in March that I'm really interested about. I'm going to miss them. But you also have the return of Avenue Q and, uh, the London production of John Proctor's the villain starting at the end of March, and it's a bit further out, but in June you have pride at the National Theatre, which is definitely on my radar as something to look out for. And if you haven't been to London in a while, there's a lot of older recommendations too that I would still toss out. Like I think Hadestown in the UK just hits different. It's great. I would always recommend HadesTown in the UK I'm probably gonna go see it again when I'm there. My neighbour Totoro is a must. It is one of the cutest things that I've ever seen, with some of the best puppetry. I cannot recommend it enough. Phantom Peak is like an immersive, interactive theatrical experience that is so much fun. I think everyone should do it at least once. But it also has infinite rewatchability so you can always go back. Anytime I go with a group we usually try to go do Phantom Peak. And I don't personally love Starlight Express, but this is a really fun production. And it is closing this year, so if you haven't seen that it may be worth a trip. But those are my top top recs for the spring. Obviously if I had to pick the highlights it would be Paddington. Harold Fry are are the top two musicals of the year.
